audit.why: TRICKY 7/10 fits a 51.96% WR artillery lane: he outranges TF at every stage, TF wins on roam tempo and pick setup.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full phases[].side disagreed with content win[] on rows 1-6 (full carried Xerath 1-4 then Skill; content/packet say TF at 2, Skill 3-5, Xerath 6 onward). Content also names his R 'Rite of the Ancients' — real name Rite of the Arcane.
audit.why: Red Card shove flips tempo at 2 by forcing him to clear; from 6 his R snipes and first-item poke zone take over — content chart matches the packet levelChart.
audit.corrected: Full sides moved to agree with content; whys rewritten; R renamed in whys[4] and spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never states that Rite of the Arcane is a self-rooting channel that TF's gold card cancels (brief missingInteractions); breakdown.cooldowns had no digits; dos/donts carried verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad.
audit.why: Xerath's R text: 'immobilizes himself', kit flag channel-interruptible — a gold card walk-up ends the barrage. Shocking Orb is 13s rank 1 / 11s max, W 14s early — real numbers for the commit window.
audit.corrected: Channel-cancel added to report[5].t, cooldown numbers added, bleed bullets rewritten.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Check it before every step-up. - W gold card is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — 13s at rank 1, 11s max, his only CC: dodge it and the artillery never converts into a kill. - His W barrage cycles every 14s early — step up between casts. The ult answers fights, not waves.

edits.before: Lock gold off-screen, walk up once, card-auto-Q, and leave — one stun-chunk per cycle is all the lane asks of you.
edits.after: Yellow card outranges nothing he has — walk up only when Shocking Orb is down, stun, Q, and get back out of his W zone.

edits.before: Cycling cards inside his engage range for stacked-deck greed — TF dies in exactly one mistimed auto-walk per game; don't pre-book it.
edits.after: He outranges you at every level — grinding poke wars mid feeds his Mana Surge farm; your gold is on the map, one Destiny at a time.

edits.before: Track Xerath’s Shocking Orb (Stun): His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Shocking Orb: his only CC — dodge it and the artillery never converts. His Rite of the Arcane self-roots as a channel: a gold card cancels it.

edits.before: W online: the gold card re-prices his every step-up. Lock yellow when he walks forward and the lane behaves.
edits.after: W online: Red Card shove forces him to clear instead of poke — your tempo, so lock yellow when he steps up.

edits.before: Full kit: stacked-deck autos plus card cycling is a real short trade — but your game is the clock, not the lane.
edits.after: Full kit: your shove-and-roam threat offsets his poke edge — level 3 belongs to whoever spaces better.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q the wave, lock cards on cooldown, and watch side lanes like they're your KDA.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay even — dodge his Q line, shove for roam windows, and watch side lanes like your KDA.

edits.before: Destiny online — THE level in this lane. Every shove is now a bot-lane death sentence with a 130-second timer.
edits.after: Destiny is online but his Rite of the Arcane snipes from screens away — roam windows now cost health to open.

edits.before: Lich Bane spike: gold card chunks half bars. The lane still isn't the point — the map pays your salary.
edits.after: His Lost Chapter spike outranges your Lich Bane one: the poke zone is permanent — take the map, not the lane.

edits.before: Late TF is a coin with two good sides: split the side lane R-safe, or hold Destiny as the pick-and-collapse button.
edits.after: Late his multi-cast R and W-Q chains zone the map — split R-safe and flank; never walk into the artillery lanes.

edits.before: At 6 his Rite of the Ancients snipes chunk you from screens away.
edits.after: At 6 his Rite of the Arcane's snipes chunk you from screens away.

edits.before: Xerath's Rite of the Ancients gives him long-range global-ish sniping while your Destiny is a roam tool; he chunks you from screens away, so use vision and roam to sidestep his artillery.
edits.after: Xerath's Rite of the Arcane gives him long-range global-ish sniping while your Destiny is a roam tool; he chunks you from screens away, so use vision and roam to sidestep his artillery.

notes: suspectNames: 'Gold Card' is TF's own W card (false positive); 'Eye of Destruction' is Xerath's real W (false positive). His R's real name is Rite of the Arcane — the content layer had 'Rite of the Ancients' twice, both fixed. The channel-cancel interaction (gold card cancels his self-rooted R) is grounded in the kit's channel flag plus the R text 'immobilizes himself' — added to report[5].t (one of the two permitted report rewrites).
